title: Landmark Circulation Publication Validates K2VITAL™ DELTA in the Largest Clinical Trial of Vitamin K2 (MK-7) and D3 for Coronary Calcification
summary: Largest vitamin K2 MK-7 and D3 trial shows K2VITAL™ DELTA slowed coronary calcification progression by 21%, published in Circulation.
body_markdown:
## **Inside DANCODE:** Vitamins K2 and D3 in Coronary Calcification


The DANCODE study confirms earlier findings from the Aortic Valve Decalcification (AVADEC) trial, and extends the potential of this vitamin pairing to both men and women.


2


In


[AVADEC](https://www.jacc.org/doi/10.1016/j.jacadv.2023.100643) , the combination was shown to slow CAC progression, which is strongly associated with a higher risk of heart disease and negative cardiovascular events, in a subgroup of men with severe coronary calcification.


2 Conducted across three Danish hospitals, this new DANCODE follow up trial enrolled both men and women of an average age of 71 with a CAC score of at least 400 Agatston units (AU) – the standard clinical measure for severe calcification. Participants received either 720 µg/day vitamin K2 MK-7, together with 25 µg/day vitamin D3, or a placebo, for 24 months.
